research_question: On MMECG, is the continuous ECG weakness partly a preprocessing artifact of the narrow 0.8-3.5 Hz bandpass, i.e. does disabling narrow_bandpass further improve the lag-aware refine model?
hypothesis: Disabling narrow_bandpass (matching the winning CR_RVS recipe) will improve fold-01 full-window (rem_full_ola) PCC over the lag-aware refine arm while preserving Shape-200 morphology.
protocol: Fold-01 strict LOSO pilot, WSST input, 30 epochs, no target-subject calibration.
changed_variable: Set narrow_bandpass=false; keep the lag-aware refine configuration otherwise fixed.
controlled_variables: MMECG processed/loso fold_01 strict LOSO split
success_criteria: Training completes for fold_01 and writes checkpoint/config/logs.
Full-window rem_full_ola PCC improves over the narrow-bandpass lag-aware arm.
Shape-200 head PCC remains near or above 0.87.
Isolate whether the continuous gain comes from lag-aware loss, wideband preprocessing, or both.
checkpoint_selection: Use the training script's validation-best checkpoint only; no test-set checkpoint selection.
failure_interpretation: If wideband does not help beyond the lag-aware arm, the narrow bandpass is not the MMECG continuous bottleneck and preprocessing should be left as-is for the 11-fold run.
